concerns.statement: The registry distinguishes observed package names, name/version identities, repeated content identities, current canonical serving objects and historical native storage; the historical count is not represented as a fresh canonical count.

The source publisher publishes exactly the source-declared edition, receives an identical existing product without minting another and refuses a changed occupied identity; git history, retry and test-only edits do not allocate an edition.

An explicit retirement lot protects installed identities and transitive closure, dist-tag targets and dependency closure, admitted incoming release dependencies, rollback products, immutable conflicts and unsettled publication input; incomplete coverage refuses only the affected retirement.

Retirement derives from the protected dependency graph and source-owned product selection rather than stable-version retention or a hardcoded count or age; PR15 is assessed, useful capability retained at the canonical R2 owner and obsolete native-only retention retired.

A retired name/version cannot be republished with same or different bytes; compact permanent identity evidence binds original integrity and source/manifest commitment without redundant payload copies or treating archived evidence as an active version.

The authenticated operator operation receives the exact metadata ETag and plan commitment, rechecks protected identities and current tags and uses original conditional storage; it never removes an advertised archive first, overwrites a concurrent publication, mutates credentials or accepts publisher-supplied retirement metadata.

The owner records intent before effects and actual conditional results after effects; interrupted removal resumes only the same lot, never overwrites or remints, distinguishes unknown effects and keeps protected packages usable; cleanup reclaims unneeded archive objects without another full copy.

Packuments, exact-version lookup, dist-tag resolution, dependency admission and archive GET/HEAD consistently exclude retired editions and retain precise retired-identity refusals; no hidden direct archive route or old native shelf bypass continues serving retired editions.

Independent receiving compares original and final canonical version counts, actual removed bytes and objects, protected exact products and archive integrities, concurrent-write refusal and interrupted-lot completion; a draft PR, deletion plan, passing synthetic suite or corrected allocator alone does not satisfy this condition.

Work17 and BCF599 retain the two disputed identities and unsettled WSL predecessor without false settlement; explicit later version retirement fulfills the current Leader request rather than silently rewriting prior conservation evidence.

The requirement is consumed by the existing Specification, Architecture, HLD, LLD and fabrication chain with exact source lineage and bounded inference; a missing generator is repaired at its existing owner and no handwritten normative code or parallel registry is introduced.

decisions.statement: Retire R2 original-input keys only under a purpose-bound retirement-lot custody distinct from publication input keys.
decisions.rationale: Prevents delayed publication cleanup from deleting a retirement claim and preserves original publisher input.

decisions.statement: Derive retirement from the protected dependency graph and source-owned product selection; retain PR15 capability at the canonical R2 owner and retire native-only retention.
decisions.rationale: Avoids hardcoded counts or ages and preserves useful capability while removing obsolete native retention.

decisions.statement: Exclude retired editions from packuments, exact lookup, dist-tag resolution, dependency admission and archive GET/HEAD; remove hidden direct archive and native shelf bypass.
decisions.rationale: Ensures consumers consistently refuse retired identities and no bypass continues serving retired editions.

decisions.statement: Protect installed, tag, admitted-incoming and rollback closure; retain Work17 and BCF599 disputed identities and WSL predecessor; consume the existing generation chain with no parallel registry.
decisions.rationale: Preserves protected identities and conservation evidence while finishing generation at the existing owner.
alternatives: Exact closure plus existing generation chain
